ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Every UBO, director, legal representative, manager, and authorized signatory must be screened before submission and continuously thereafter against the United Nations Security Council consolidated lists, China's Ministry of Foreign Affairs designations, the MOFCOM Unreliable Entity List, and the OFAC SDN and non-SDN lists wherever USD clearing, US correspondent banking, or US market access is involved. EU and UK consolidated financial sanctions lists must also be screened where alternative payment rails are used. PEPs, including mainland Chinese government and state-owned enterprise officials, Taiwan political figures, and their close associates, require enhanced due diligence, source of wealth and source of funds verification, senior management approval, and increased ongoing transaction monitoring under the PRC Anti-Money Laundering Law and FATF Recommendations. Automated risk scoring must flag any sanction hit, PEP status, adverse media, litigation, insolvency, or negative reputation item and pause the incorporation until the matter is cleared.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: SAMR National Enterprise Name Registration System (State Administration for Market Regulation online name application and reservation portal)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The registered legal name must be in Chinese script and follow the mandatory four-tier structure: [administrative division] + [distinctive trade name] + [industry characterization] + [company form 'Co., Ltd.']. Roman letters, Arabic numerals, punctuation, and foreign words are prohibited in the registered Chinese name. A phonetic pinyin transliteration may be used as a non-registered English reference name only and carries no legal registration effect.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If a name application is rejected, the applicant should: (1) access the SAMR name registration portal and download the official rejection notice containing the refusal code; (2) within 15 calendar days, submit a written administrative appeal to the same SAMR department through the online portal or in person, attaching the rejection notice, a corrected proposed name, business scope, investor identity, and a legal argument against the refusal; (3) SAMR must respond within 10 working days; (4) if the appeal is refused, the applicant may apply for administrative reconsideration to the superior SAMR authority within 60 days, then pursue an administrative lawsuit in a competent People's Court within 6 months. A name reservation may be extended once for another 30 days before expiry.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Company Act of Taiwan (公司法), Articles 1, 2, 18, 98-113, 128-137, 172, 192, 208, 235, 266-267; Foreign Investment Act (Taiwan), Articles 1-7; Factories Management Act, Article 13; Rules Governing Approval of Foreign Investment and the Verification of Paid-in Capital
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Ministry of Economic Affairs (MOEA), Investment Commission for foreign investment approval; Department of Commercial Affairs (MOEA) for company registration; local National Taxation Bureau, Ministry of Finance for tax registration
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Company Registration Application Form and Articles of Incorporation together with a CPA capital verification report and Foreign Investment Approval Letter
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: None. Taiwan imposes no minimum paid-up capital for a limited company. For a WFOE, the foreign shareholder must remit the full subscribed capital from abroad into a Taiwan bank account in the company's name, report the remittance to the Central Bank through a designated bank, and obtain a CPA capital verification report before registration. No blocked escrow account is required, but the capital must remain deposited in the company's Taiwan account and may not be disbursed until registration is completed.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Foreign Investment Approval and WFOE Eligibility Clearance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Investment Commission, Ministry of Economic Affairs (MOEA), Taiwan - Online Cloud Application System
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the foreign investment application through the MOEA Investment Commission cloud application system, selecting the investment project code for synthetic resin and plastics product manufacturing. Attach the parent company's certificate of incorporation, audited financial statements for the latest fiscal year, a board resolution authorizing the Taiwan investment, notarized identity certificates of the shareholders and ultimate beneficial owner, and a business plan covering ISIC 3240 polyresin vacuum casting, hand painting, and garage-kit assembly. The plan must state the planned factory address, installed power, production capacity, resin and solvent storage volumes, and waste disposal procedures. After submission, pay the application fee and obtain a filing receipt. The Commission will review the application for compliance with negative lists and statute restrictions. If approved, the Commission will issue a Foreign Investment Approval Letter, which is valid for one year for capital remittance and company registration.
required_dossiers: Parent company certificate of incorporation and board resolution
Audited financial statements of the foreign investor for the last fiscal year
Passport/corporate identity documents of shareholders and UBO
Business plan for resin statue manufacturing
Power of attorney for local agent (if any)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a query or suspension notice is issued, file a written supplementary explanation with the Investment Commission within 14 days. If the application is denied, cure the stated legal deficiency and resubmit a new application; alternatively, appeal to the Executive Yuan under the Administrative Appeal Act within 30 days of the denial.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Capital Remittance, Bank Account Opening, and CPA Paid-In Capital Verification
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Designated foreign exchange bank in Taiwan, Central Bank of Taiwan, and a Taiwan-licensed Certified Public Accountant
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a New Taiwan Dollar deposit account and a foreign currency account in the proposed company name with a designated bank using the Foreign Investment Approval Letter and the proposed Articles of Incorporation. The overseas shareholder must remit the subscribed capital from its own overseas account with the remittance purpose code for foreign investment. The bank shall issue a Foreign Exchange Transaction Certificate or a credit notification evidencing the inflow. Engage a Taiwan-licensed CPA to prepare the Capital Verification Report in accordance with the Rules Governing the Verification of Paid-in Capital, attaching the bank statement, remittance certificate, and articles of incorporation. All original instruments must be retained and submitted with the company registration application. No blocked escrow account is needed, and the capital may not be returned to the shareholder before the company is registered.
required_dossiers: Bank account opening forms and company seal
Overseas remittance instruction and transaction certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank flags an incorrect remittance purpose code or the amount is lower than subscribed, request the overseas remitter to issue a correcting remittance or obtain a written reconciliation from the bank. If the CPA identifies a discrepancy in the bank records, cure the bank documentation and have the CPA reissue the verification report before the company registration application is filed.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Name Reservation and Company Registration Filing with Ministry of Economic Affairs
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Department of Commercial Affairs, Ministry of Economic Affairs (MOEA), Taiwan - One-Stop Company Registration Service
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: First reserve the company name with the MOEA online name reservation system. After reservation, prepare and file the Company Registration Application Form with the Department of Commercial Affairs, attaching the Articles of Incorporation signed by all promoters, the Foreign Investment Approval Letter, the CPA Capital Verification Report, a registered-office lease agreement with the building owner's written consent, the identity certificate of the responsible person, and the list of directors and shareholders. Pay the application fee and obtain the filing receipt. The Department will review the filing under the Company Act and, if satisfactory, issue a Company Registration Certificate. After company registration, the same application may trigger the business tax registration; however, the National Taxation Bureau registration is requested separately in step 4.
required_dossiers: Lease agreement and owner's consent for registered office
Identity documents of directors, shareholders and responsible person
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the MOEA issues a query or suspension, respond through the One-Stop Service portal within 15 days by amending the Articles of Incorporation, correcting the registered address, or supplementing consent letters. If the filing is rejected, file a corrected application and pay the fee again; administrative appeal to the Executive Yuan is available within 30 days of rejection.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax Registration and Uniform Invoice Issuance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: National Taxation Bureau of the relevant tax district, Ministry of Finance, Taiwan
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within 15 days after the company registration certificate is obtained, file the Business Tax Registration Application and the Profit-Seeking Enterprise Income Tax Registration with the local National Taxation Bureau. Submit the company registration certificate, the responsible person's identity documents, the registered-office lease, and the company seal. The National Taxation Bureau will issue a tax registration identification number and authorize the use of Uniform Invoices. Purchase a Uniform Invoice from the certified printer and apply for the Uniform Invoice Vendor Seal. This step is mandatory before the company may issue invoices for preorder deposits received via Stripe or PayPal. If the company expects to be a zero-rated exporter of resin statues, register the export status and report monthly VAT returns under Article 39 of the Value-Added and Non-value-Added Business Tax Act.
required_dossiers: Responsible person's ID and seal card
Lease agreement for the business premises
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the tax authority asks for clarification, provide the requested documents within 10 days. If a late registration penalty is imposed, file a statement of reasons and apply for abatement; if the Uniform Invoice issuance is blocked, correct the vendor seal application and obtain the final approval before issuing any invoice.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Factory Registration, Labor Insurance, Health Insurance, and Commencement of Manufacturing
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Industrial Development Administration, MOEA; local municipal/county government economic development bureau; Ministry of Labor; National Health Insurance Administration
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: If the resin statue production site meets the thresholds under the Factories Management Act, apply for a Factory Registration Certificate before commencing manufacturing. Submit the factory floor plans, building-use certificate, fire safety inspection report, land-use entitlement proof, and a list of manufacturing equipment. In parallel, register the company with the Ministry of Labor for labor insurance, occupational accident insurance, and labor pension; and register employees with the National Health Insurance Administration. File material safety data sheets for all resins, hardeners, and thinners and establish the occupational exposure protection program. Only after the factory certificate and insurance registrations are completed may production and hiring begin.
required_dossiers: Building usage certificate and structural inspection report
Fire safety certification (from local fire department)
Material safety data sheets for resins and solvents
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If factory registration is suspended, cure the zoning, building-use, or fire safety deficiency within 60 days and resubmit the revised plans. If insurance registration is rejected, obtain a corrected company registration certificate and re-file. An administrative appeal to the MOEA or the competent municipal government is available within 30 days of the adverse decision.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Industrial Development Administration (IDA), Ministry of Economic Affairs (MOEA), Taiwan; local municipality/county government economic development bureau; Ministry of Environment (Taiwan) for environmental permits; local fire department for fire safety certification
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Factory Registration Certificate under the Factories Management Act; Fixed Pollution Source Construction/Operation Permit under the Air Pollution Control Act; Hazardous Waste Generation/Storage Registration under the Waste Disposal Act

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministry of Environment, Taiwan (formerly Environmental Protection Administration)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category II - Environmental Registration; no Full EIA Report is required if the factory site is below the Category I thresholds of the Development Activities EIA Determination Standards (below 5 hectares and below 10 MW installed power). If the installed electrical capacity is 10 MW or more, or the site is 5 hectares or more, a Full Environmental Impact Assessment Report and approval must be obtained before construction. For a small workshop, an Environmental Management Registration and pollution prevention plan are still required.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Wastewater from mold cleaning and casting operations must meet Taiwan Effluent Standards: pH 6.0-9.0, biochemical oxygen demand (BOD5) not exceeding 30 mg/L, chemical oxygen demand (COD) not exceeding 100 mg/L, and suspended solids (SS) not exceeding 30 mg/L. For air emission sources, total organic solvent emissions from painting/casting operations must be assessed; if a single source emits more than 0.6 kg/hour of total organic compounds or 25 metric tons per year of VOCs, a Fixed Pollution Source Construction/Operation Permit is required together with activated carbon or regenerative thermal oxidizer abatement achieving at least 85% removal efficiency. Hazardous waste generated from resin casting and painting, including waste resin monomers, hardeners, solvent-contaminated rags, paint sludge, and spent activated carbon, must be classified as hazardous industrial waste, stored in leak-proof labeled containers, retained for no longer than 180 days at the factory, and delivered to licensed waste treatment operators. All discharge and waste manifest records must be retained for at least three years.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire Safety Certification must be obtained from the local fire department under the Fire Services Act, including approval of evacuation routes, fire extinguishers, emergency lighting, and flammable-liquid storage cabinets for Class B liquids. If the workshop stores more than 200 liters of flammable solvents, a Fire and Explosion Prevention operating permit is required. A structural load inspection certificate from a licensed structural engineer must cover the casting floor and warehouse mezzanine. Occupational safety approval from the Ministry of Labor under the Occupational Safety and Health Act requires ventilated spray booths, chemical exposure monitoring for styrene/acrylate vapors, emergency eye wash stations and showers, personal protective equipment, and a hazard communication program with material safety data sheets. The workplace must pass a Ministry of Labor inspection before the first hires are exposed to resin casting operations.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Ministry of Finance, Taxation Administration (Taiwan), acting regionally through the National Taxation Bureaus; exporters are additionally registered with the Customs Administration, Ministry of Finance. The online electronic tax portal used for filing and invoice registration is the Ministry of Finance Electronic Tax Filing and Payment Service Platform, together with the Cloud Invoice E-Invoice Integrated Service Platform for electronic uniform invoices.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign non-resident entity establishing a Taiwan Wholly Foreign-Owned Enterprise (WFOE) must first obtain incorporation approval from the Department of Commercial Services, Ministry of Economic Affairs (MOEA) under the Company Act. There is no minimum paid-in capital requirement. After company registration is approved, the WFOE must apply in writing to the local National Taxation Bureau for tax registration, submitting the company registration certificate, articles of incorporation, foreign investor identification, resident manager identification, and proof of business premises. The National Taxation Bureau then assigns the eight-digit Unified Business Number (UB), which is the sole statutory Taxpayer Identification Number and VAT registration number. The WFOE must separately complete Uniform Invoice registration with the same tax bureau, electing either paper uniform invoices or MOF-approved electronic uniform invoices via the Cloud Invoice E-Invoice Integrated Service Platform. For export trade, the WFOE must also complete customs registration and obtain an exporter code from the Customs Administration, Ministry of Finance. All subsequent changes to name, address, responsible person, or business scope must be filed with the National Taxation Bureau within the statutory change period.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation; a Taiwan WFOE is a resident profit-seeking enterprise taxed at the entity level and is not eligible for pass-through treatment.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None; Taiwan has no check-the-box election or hybrid mismatch election comparable to United States or OECD models. A WFOE is automatically subject to entity-level profit-seeking enterprise income tax. For indirect tax purposes only, an enterprise may be classified as a small-scale business subject to the 1% special business tax if its average monthly sales are below TWD 200,000 and the tax authority approves, but this is a statutory special regime, not an entity classification election.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value-added and Non-value-added Business Tax Act (Taiwan Business Tax / VAT)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No minimum threshold applies to a WFOE; all profit-seeking enterprises must apply for tax registration before commencing operations. For Taiwanese business tax purposes, a sales-of-goods business with average monthly turnover below TWD 80,000 and a sales-of-services business with average monthly turnover below TWD 40,000 may be eligible for exemption from tax registration; businesses with average monthly turnover below TWD 200,000 may qualify as small-scale businesses taxed at 1%, while standard VAT registration, 5% output VAT, and Uniform Invoice issuance are mandatory when monthly taxable turnover reaches TWD 200,000 or where the entity is a limited company such as a WFOE.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Taiwan does not operate a real-time fiscal clearance or digital stamping mandate comparable to Latin American models. Standard VAT taxpayers must issue Uniform Invoices for all taxable sales. When electronic invoicing is used, the WFOE must integrate with the Ministry of Finance Cloud Invoice E-Invoice Integrated Service Platform using the Electronic Invoice Turnkey service, transmitting encrypted invoice data, including the eight-digit Unified Business Number, invoice sequential number, and random check code, within the required filing period. The Turnkey API supports invoice registration, voiding, replacement, and query operations; paper uniform invoices remain acceptable but must be sourced from the National Taxation Bureau-approved printer and reported in the periodic VAT return.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Under Article 7 of the Value-added and Non-value-added Business Tax Act, a supply of goods qualifies for 0% VAT where the goods are physically exported from Taiwan customs territory to a foreign destination, the export sale is evidenced by an accepted Customs Export Declaration, the seller retains the complete shipping and commercial documentation chain, and the export proceeds are received from the foreign buyer through the authorized foreign-exchange banking system. Qualifying offshore digital services may also be zero-rated where the services are supplied to e-commerce consumers or business customers abroad, provided the contract, payment records, and usage evidence demonstrate the service is rendered for use outside Taiwan and no part of the supply is consumed in Taiwan. The 0% rate differs from exemption in that input VAT on export-related purchases remains creditable and refundable.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (export customs Bill of Entry equivalent) bearing the customs declaration number, exporter name, consignee, commodity code, quantity, unit price, and clearance status
Commercial Invoice and signed Sales Contract or Purchase Order reflecting the foreign buyer, Incoterms, currency, delivery terms, and total export consideration
Ocean Bill of Lading or Airway Bill evidencing shipment from a Taiwan port or airport to the overseas destination

Bank Foreign Exchange Receipts and Settlement Certificate or Inward Remittance Certificate (FIRC) issued by an authorized foreign-exchange bank in Taiwan proving that the export proceeds were received from abroad and repatriated
Customs-approved e-export declaration records and any applicable zero-rated schedule filed in the periodic VAT return
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The National Taxation Bureau and Customs Administration will review the correlation between the export declaration, transport documents, payment records, and the amounts reported as zero-rated exports. If the foreign exchange is not received within 180 days from shipment or the supporting documentation is missing, false, or inconsistent, the zero-rating is denied and the export sale is reclassified as a domestic taxable sale subject to the standard 5% VAT. The authorities will also claw back any previously refunded input VAT and impose late interest. Administrative penalties are assessed under the penalty provisions of the Value-added and Non-value-added Business Tax Act, generally up to five times the amount of tax underpaid; serious cases involving counterfeit declarations, forged documents, or intentional tax evasion may be referred for criminal tax evasion prosecution, and the statutory collection period for retroactive assessment is up to seven years from the filing date.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Central Bank of the Republic of China (Taiwan) (CBC)
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Taiwan operates an open but managed foreign exchange regime. The New Taiwan Dollar (TWD) is fully convertible for current-account transactions, including trade in goods and services, and for most capital-account transactions, subject to prior approval from the CBC unless falling under statutory automatic approval categories. There are no surrender requirements for export proceeds, and exporters may hold their foreign currency receipts in authorized bank foreign-currency deposit accounts or convert them to TWD at their discretion. However, profit remittance to overseas shareholders, especially to a Chinese parent under the cross-strait context, requires a tax clearance certificate issued by the Taiwan National Taxation Bureau, a verified audited financial statement, and a board resolution confirming dividend distribution. For inbound capital investment from the People's Republic of China, the remittance must also clear both PRC SAFE outbound investment review and Taiwan's Investment Commission (MOEA) approval. While Taiwan does not impose compulsory conversion ratios, remittance of more than NT$500,000 per transaction or equivalent must be filed with the CBC through authorized banks, and a cumulative annual filing is required for larger flows. The legal currency regime is stable, but cross-strait political factors may slow high-value remittances, making advance planning and staggered transfers prudent for liquidity management.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Under Taiwan's Foreign Exchange Control Act and Central Bank administrative directions, all export proceeds in foreign currency must be repatriated to Taiwan within six months from the date of shipment or performance of the service, unless the authorized bank grants an extension under unusual circumstances. There is no mandatory conversion ratio; enterprises may keep the proceeds in a foreign-currency account at a licensed domestic bank or sell them for TWD through authorized banks. The exporter must present the customs declaration, invoice, packing list, and a foreign-exchange settlement contract to the bank, and the bank must report all settlements to the Central Bank's Foreign Exchange Reporting System, including transaction purpose codes and supporting documents, according to the 'Report on Foreign Exchange Settlement by Banks' regulations. Failure to meet the repatriation deadline without prior application exposes the exporter to administrative penalties and potential CBC-directed compliance audits.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account (Investment) and Basic Operational Multi-Currency Account (TWD/USD)
Basic Operational Currency Account with linked Foreign Currency Deposit Account (TWD/USD/CNH)
Corporate Operational Account with Trade Finance Module and FX Forward Revaluation Line

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Taiwan's Financial Supervisory Commission (FSC) requires any entity providing payment, e-money, or corporate deposit services to be licensed under the Electronic Payment Institution Act or the Banking Act. Offshore digital EMI providers such as Revolut, N26, or global neobanks without a Taiwan branch are legally barred from opening corporate bank accounts or holding deposits for Taiwan-incorporated entities. International payment processors like Stripe and PayPal may operate as cross-border acquirers in Taiwan only through licensed local banks or payment institutions, and they are permitted solely for collecting customer payments on behalf of the seller — not for treasury liquidity management, FX hedging, or multi-currency clearing. Therefore, the viability of using offshore EMIs as the primary banking rail is low for this WFOE. For day-to-day treasury operations, we recommend pairing a Tier-1 domestic Taiwanese bank for corporate banking and FX with a licensed PSP such as Stripe or PayPal for preorder-driven e-commerce collections. The entity may open a Stripe account in Taiwan using its local company certificate and bank account, but settlement will be in TWD or converted to the linked bank currency; no dedicated FX hedging can be executed through the PSP.

stage_4.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Statutory directors and Taiwan-registered legal representatives must appear physically in person at the bank's head office or a domestic designated branch to complete the corporate account opening interview. The CBC's anti-money laundering rules require financial institutions to verify the identity of all beneficial owners, directors, and authorized signatories through face-to-face consultation. A remote consular proxy opening is not permitted for a new WFOE; however, if a director resides overseas, the bank may allow a notarized board resolution and, in limited cases, a video interview for the overseas director, provided at least one full authorised representative physically attends at the Taiwan branch. For Chinese parent-company directors, the bank will additionally require a copy of the approved outward investment certificate from SAFE and a mainland passport with in-town stamp arrival to evidence the person's presence in Taiwan at the time of the interview. Physical attendance is a mandatory prerequisite for obtaining online banking tokens and transaction signing permissions.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cross-strait geopolitical sensitivity: ultimate beneficial owners are PRC citizens and the company is 100% owned by a mainland Chinese parent, triggering enhanced due diligence under Taiwan's AML/CFT framework.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Full corporate extraction summary from Taiwan's company registry and PRC business registration; complete UBO org chart with certified passport copies of all natural persons holding >10%; documented source of wealth (tax returns, payroll records, dividend distribution statements, sale of assets); declaration and supporting evidence that no UBO is on the PRC military-civilian fusion or Taiwan-related sanctions list; detailed business plan for the resin statue manufacturing and international e-commerce operations, including expected transaction volumes and counterparty geographies.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High volume of global preorder deposits collected through Stripe/PayPal with a clear mismatch between when funds arrive and when goods are physically shipped, creating potential for layering under trade-based money laundering typologies.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Audited transaction log from Stripe and PayPal covering at least the past 12 months, mapping each preorder to the corresponding customer order number; warehouse inventory records and serial numbers for the resin statues; shipping logs with courier tracking numbers (DHL/FedEx/etc.) and customs entry declarations proving eventual physical export; refund and chargeback historical policy documents; a written internal control statement describing the separation between the deposit collection function and the manufacturing inventory system.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Capital injection from mainland China into Taiwan without clear evidence of having obtained both PRC SAFE and Taiwan MOEA Investment Commission approvals, which is a common violation when using offshore pass-through structures.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: SAFE Foreign Exchange Certificate for Outbound Investment (or eligible ODI filing); Taiwan MOEA Investment Commission approval letter for the inward investment; bank-to-bank SWIFT MT103 records with clean narrative excluding round-tripping or multi-hop channels; CPA capital verification report from a licensed Taiwan accountant; board resolutions of both parent and subsidiary approving the capital injection; evidence of the actual remittance being funded from the parent's operating cash flow rather than from a third-party intermediary.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Selected ISIC 3240 (resin toy and statue manufacturing) has a niche trade profile that may involve licensed IP, copyright, and permission from franchise holders; an unexpected third-party intellectual property dispute could indicate the company is being used as a conduit for royalty evasion or illegal product distribution.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Copy of the trademark or parental licensing agreement (if any) authorising the manufacturing of the resin statues; evidence of royalty payments to licensors, if applicable; photograph and description of the design provenance; completed customs IPR declarations; legal opining from a Taiwan attorney on the company's compliance with the Intellectual Property Act and the Fun/Toys product safety regulation; a list of all subcontractors who may have access to the moulds and paint applications.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Shareholders' Meeting Approval of Business Report, Financial Statements, and Profit Distribution Proposal, followed by filing to the Ministry of Economic Affairs
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Ministry of Economic Affairs (MOEA), Department of Commercial Affairs; meeting is held at shareholder level
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 6 months after fiscal year-end, i.e., on or before June 30 of the following calendar year; may be extended only with competent authority approval
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Responsible directors may be fined NT$20,000–NT$100,000 (approx. US$620–US$3,100) and ordered by MOEA to convene the meeting; shareholders may petition to cause the meeting; repeated non-compliance may lead to compulsory dissolution proceedings. Taiwan does not operate an automatic administrative strike-off regime.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Profit-Seeking Enterprise Income Tax Return, including undistributed earnings surtax where applicable
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Taxation Bureau, Ministry of Finance, Taiwan
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before May 31 of the calendar year following fiscal year-end; the deadline shifts to the next business day if May 31 is a weekend/holiday
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing surcharge of 10% of the payable tax if filed after the deadline before investigation, rising to 15% if assessed by the tax authority; underpayment penalties up to 15% plus daily late-payment interest; wilful evasion may trigger criminal liability under the Tax Collection Act.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Foreign Investor Operational Report for the Wholly Foreign-Owned Enterprise capital structure
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Investment Commission, Ministry of Economic Affairs (MOEAIC), Taiwan
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 6 months after fiscal year-end, i.e., on or before June 30 of the following calendar year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative warning and correction order; persistent failure may suspend foreign exchange remittance privileges, future capital repatriation approvals, and in aggravated cases may lead to revocation of the foreign investment approval after due notice. No automatic strike-off applies.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory independent certified public accountant audit is triggered for a non-public Taiwan company when paid-in capital exceeds NT$30,000,000 or annual operating revenue exceeds NT$30,000,000; public companies and listed entities are subject to Financial Supervisory Commission audit requirements under the Securities and Exchange Act.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Public companies: Taiwan Financial Reporting Standards (TIFRS, fully converged with IFRS as endorsed by the FSC). Non-public companies and WFOEs: Business Entity Accounting Act, Related Regulations, and Taiwan Financial Reporting Standards for non-public entities.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Under Company Act Article 22-1, the WFOE must report directors, supervisors, managers, and major shareholders holding more than 10% of outstanding shares to the MOEA information platform within 15 days of incorporation or any change; no separate annual UBO confirmation return exists, but every shareholding transfer must be reflected in the statutory register and reported to MOEA within 15 days; the register must be available for inspection at the annual shareholders' meeting.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Minute Book (Shareholders' Meeting Minutes and Board Meeting Minutes)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: US$350–US$1,200 per year for registered office, statutory secretarial/agent, and basic compliance support
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: US$6,000–US$15,000 per year for a certified independent audit of a mid-sized manufacturing WFOE; lower-end fee applies where only financial statement compilation or review is permitted.
